summary: GitHub OAuth app setup is self-serve: create the app in Developer settings, then request only the scopes your agent needs, usually `repo` plus `workflow` or webhook scopes when those features are required. The main catch is that OAuth scopes are coarse, and some organizations must approve OAuth apps before members can connect them.
difficultyReason: Anyone with a GitHub account can register an OAuth app in minutes and real users can connect right away. GitHub does not review OAuth apps. Two things can still slow you down: organizations that turn on OAuth app access restrictions must approve your app before it can see their data, and GitHub limits OAuth apps to 2,000 access token requests per hour.

timeToProduction.text: Same day for personal accounts; longer if an organization owner must approve access

requirements.text: Create the OAuth app under a personal account or an organization you administer.
requirements.quote: You can create and register an OAuth app under your personal account or under any organization you have administrative access to.
Only use information in your OAuth app that you consider public.
OAuth apps need to request the repo scope

requirements.text: Use `write:repo_hook` if you need webhook-driven repository triggers.
requirements.quote: OAuth apps request the webhook scope

requirements.text: Add `workflow` if the agent will create or update GitHub Actions workflow files.
requirements.quote: add and update GitHub Actions workflow files.

requirements.text: Add `offline_access` if you want refresh tokens for expiring access tokens.
requirements.quote: Requests an expiring access token and a refresh token

requirements.text: Users must verify their primary email before authorizing.
requirements.quote: You must verify your email address before you can authorize an OAuth app.

reviewTriggers.text: If the target organization has OAuth app access restrictions enabled, an owner must approve access.
reviewTriggers.quote: organization members and outside collaborators must request approval from an organization owner

reviewTriggers.text: If you publish the app in GitHub Marketplace, GitHub requires listing verification.
reviewTriggers.quote: you must request verification for the app listing.

reviewTriggers.text: Paid OAuth app listings need at least 200 users.
reviewTriggers.quote: OAuth apps should have a minimum of 200 users.

steps.title: Open Developer settings and start a new app
steps.detail: Go to GitHub Settings, then Developer settings > OAuth apps, and click New OAuth App.
steps.quote: click your profile picture, then click Settings.

steps.title: Set the callback URL
steps.detail: Paste the exact redirect URL you will use. Leave `redirect_uri` out unless you need to override the default callback.

steps.title: User authorizes the app
steps.detail: Send the user through GitHub's consent screen and exchange the returned code for a token.
steps.quote: Once the user has authorized, the app will receive an access token

steps.title: Get org owner approval when needed
steps.detail: If the target organization restricts OAuth apps, an owner has to review the request and grant access.
steps.quote: organization members and outside collaborators must request approval from an organization owner

blockers.problem: The callback URL does not match GitHub's registered callback URL.
blockers.whatToDo: Use the exact registered callback URL, or omit `redirect_uri` and let GitHub use the first saved callback URL.
blockers.quote: The redirect_uri MUST match the registered callback URL for this application.

blockers.problem: GitHub throttles token minting if the app keeps re-running authorization.
blockers.whatToDo: Cache tokens and avoid re-running the OAuth flow on every request.
blockers.quote: OAuth apps are subject to a rate limit of 2,000 access token requests per hour.

blockers.problem: Deleted access tokens do not clean up webhook subscriptions automatically.
blockers.whatToDo: Plan a manual cleanup path for repository or organization webhooks when users disconnect the app.
blockers.quote: Webhooks are not automatically disabled if an OAuth app's access token is deleted

agentDrafts.title: App description
agentDrafts.text: Connect your GitHub account so the AI agent can read repository data and perform authorized write actions like creating issues, pull requests, comments, and webhook-driven updates on your behalf.

agentDrafts.title: Scope justification: repo
agentDrafts.text: Needed so the agent can read and write repository content, issues, pull requests, and other repo-owned data for the connected user.

agentDrafts.title: Scope justification: webhook triggers
agentDrafts.text: Needed so GitHub can send repository events to the app instead of the agent polling for changes.

agentDrafts.title: Scope justification: workflow
agentDrafts.text: Needed only if the agent will create or update GitHub Actions workflow files.

Do you need private email addresses from GitHub? If yes, add `user:email`.
